conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you during this admission. Can you tell me what brought you in today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve been having sharp pain in my upper abdomen, constant nausea, and dizziness when I stand. I threw up once—greenish, not bloody. I haven’t eaten much—just a little pudding yesterday morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay, that sounds similar to your past episodes. You’ve had several hospitalizations recently for partial bowel obstructions, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, five in the last three months. I was just discharged two days ago on a full liquid diet, but the pain and nausea came back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. We reviewed your CT scan from today. It shows no major change from the one five days ago. There’s still a piece of old tubing in your small bowel that might be causing irritation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The tubing from my old GJ tube? I thought that might be the issue.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. The scan shows new wall thickening around that area, which could be contributing to the partial obstruction. But there’s no sign of a complete blockage or free air, so surgery isn’t needed right now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what’s the plan? I’m so tired of being sick.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll continue with bowel rest—no food by mouth for now. You’ll get fluids through an IV, and we’ll manage your nausea with Phenergan and your pain with your usual morphine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my G-tube? It’s been draining a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll keep it to gravity drainage, not suction. It’s helping decompress your stomach. Also, we’ve scheduled to replace the G-tube tomorrow—it was already planned, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s been leaking a bit. I’m glad we’re doing that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. The procedure is low-risk and will be done under fluoroscopy to make sure the new tube is placed correctly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Still nauseous, but the pain is a little less. I’m really weak and dizzy when I try to sit up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood pressure was low this morning—75 over 51 when you stood. That explains the dizziness. We’re giving you more IV fluids to help with dehydration.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been dizzy for months, but it’s worse now. Is that from the bowel issue?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Partly. Dehydration and not eating are making it worse. We’ll keep monitoring it. Your labs show your hemoglobin is a bit low, but stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my INR? I’m on Coumadin.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your PTT was high on admission—150—but it’s coming down. We’ll check it again soon. No bleeding, so we’re continuing your warfarin at the same dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re about to take you for your G-tube replacement. Any questions before we go?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt? How long does it take?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll get some sedation, so you’ll be relaxed. It usually takes about 30 minutes. They’ll confirm the placement with contrast to make sure it’s in the stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The procedure went perfectly. The new G-tube is in place, and the contrast confirmed it’s in the stomach. You did great.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I feel a little pressure, but no pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s normal. We’ll keep it clamped for a bit, then start with gravity drainage. Once you’re stable, we’ll try advancing your diet.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—your nausea has improved, and the G-tube output has decreased. We’re going to try starting you on clear liquids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have some broth or apple juice?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll start with small amounts. We’ll also clamp the G-tube for 45 minutes after each intake to see how you tolerate it without drainage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You did well with the liquids. No vomiting, and the clamp test was successful. We’re going to advance to full liquids—like yogurt, pudding, and Ensure.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That sounds good. I’m hungry. But I’m worried about the Ensure—won’t that affect my phosphate?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good point. Your phosphate was high this morning—6.3. You’ll need to take two TUMS with each bottle of Ensure to bind the phosphate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And my other labs?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your white count is normal, no infection. Liver and kidney function are stable. We’ll check your INR and phosphate again before discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been on full liquids for over 24 hours with no issues. The G-tube has been clamped, and you’re not needing suction. That’s a big improvement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I feel much better. Can I go home soon?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, if all goes well today, we’re planning to discharge you tomorrow. You’ll stay on full liquids and follow up with your GI doctor before trying solids.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What about my meds? Are they changing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No major changes. We’re increasing your trazodone to 150 mg at bedtime for sleep. Everything else stays the same, including your warfarin and thyroid meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the Phenergan for nausea?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll keep that as needed, especially before meals. We’re sending home 120 tablets.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your latest INR is 2.8—perfect for warfarin. Phosphate is 5.9, so still a bit high. Keep taking TUMS with Ensure and limit to three bottles a day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll do that. When do I get the lab work done?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll have blood drawn three days after discharge to check INR and phosphate. Call your primary doctor with the results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done really well. Vital signs are stable, pain is controlled, and you’ve tolerated full liquids without nausea. We’re ready to discharge you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What should I watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Call your doctor or go to the ER if you have fever, severe abdominal pain, vomiting, or shortness of breath. Otherwise, keep on full liquids and follow up with GI in a week.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my G-tube site? Any signs of infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep it clean and dry. If it becomes red, swollen, or starts draining pus, let us know. Right now, it looks clean and healing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate all the care.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a quick check before you leave. How are you feeling?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Tired but much better. Ready to be home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. Remember: full liquids, TUMS with Ensure, no solids yet, and follow up with GI. We’ll send your discharge papers now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Nurse will be in shortly with your prescriptions and instructions. Any last questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I think I’ve got it all. Thank you again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Take it slow at home and call if anything changes.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just confirming—you’ve reviewed the discharge instructions and have all your meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, everything’s here. I’ll follow up with my doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Excellent. You’re cleared to go home. Rest well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: One last thing—your dizziness has improved, but be careful when standing. Rise slowly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve been doing that the last few days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. Keep up the progress.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Transport is here to take you home. We’re glad you’re feeling better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I really appreciate it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just checking in one last time. All set to go?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, all set. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.
